Claudia: quick follow-up from the KV-cache OOM postmortem. we need concrete owners, short delivery windows, and a repeatable verification plan. dropping a compact action list — ack & add ETA here.

Claudia: action list: (A) continuous jemalloc + slab profiling on canary, (B) compaction GC tuning + scheduled compaction job, (C) strict memory limits + graceful fallback path, (D) nightly OOM/regression check + alerting, (E) root-cause: investigate Wed early-morning fragmentation spike.

Ravi: I'll pick A. plan: enable jemalloc stats + periodic heap dumps on canary for 48h, collect slab histograms and large-object maps. ETA: Wed EOD. need a safe capture script to avoid CPU spike.

Ravi: capture script (draft):
```bash
# run on canary node, low-priority
sudo cgexec -g cpu:low nice -n 10 /usr/local/bin/collect-jemalloc.sh --pid $(pidof redwood-runtime) --out /tmp/dumps
# then upload
aws s3 cp /tmp/dumps s3://redwood-incidents/1799650000/ --recursive
```

Marisol: I'll take B. proposed tuning: lower max_cache_retention from 12h -> 4h on canary, enable background_compact=true, and add a scheduled compaction at Sat 03:30 UTC (post-backup window). I'll add CPU/priority circuit-breakers. ETA: 10 days for PR + canary rollout.

Jon: I'll own D (regression/nightly). plan: nightly canary job that runs worst-case prompts + mem-check harness, compare 95p usage to golden baseline, and create auto-ticket if regression > 15%. ETA: 5 days for baseline + alerting.

Claudia: C (limits + fallback) still unassigned. we need a runtime enforcement layer so processes gracefully reject new heavy requests instead of OOM. also a library-level hook to offload large KV items to disk. who can pick?

sre-oncall: I can prototype a soft limiter that returns 429 with Retry-After when cache mem% > 85%. small risk to client experience but prevents node death. ETA: 3 days for PoC.

Claudia: excellent. assign to sre-oncall for PoC; follow-on will be product/SDK changes.

InfraBot: note: backup snapshot today (1799647200) duration 35m; correlated with a memory spike window in canary. repeating pattern Wed 03:00 UTC and Sat 03:00 UTC.

Marisol: to avoid compaction overlap with backups I'll schedule compaction at Sat 03:30 UTC and add a pre-check: run only if last-backup-age > 1h. sample YAML for compaction job (will PR):
```yaml
compaction:
  enabled: true
  schedule: '30 3 * * 6' # Sat 03:30 UTC
  cpu_threshold: 60
  precondition: last_backup_age_seconds > 3600
  max_runtime: '25m'
  priority: low
```

Ravi: for profiling please also capture 'kvctl slab-stats --json' and hotspot key list. I'll annotate large-key patterns and correlate with jemalloc fragmentation.

Jon: testing detail: nightly harness will include: (1) synthetic hot-keys churn, (2) long-tail huge value inserts, (3) prefix scan worst-case. will post test vectors in the ticket.

Claudia: recap of owners & short ETAs: Ravi (A profiling) 48h, Marisol (B compaction/tuning) 10d, Jon (D nightly/regression) d, sre-oncall (C soft limiter PoC) d. I'll update postmortem and create follow-up sub-tasks in the incident board.

deploy-bot: planned canary: redwood/runtime@canary -> 1799650600.

Ravi: uploading initial dumps now -> https://s3.redwood/1799650000/ ; will add a README with capture times.

Marisol: PR for compaction config coming shortly; will include circuit-breaker logic to skip if CPU>60 or backup_recent.

sre-oncall: once PoC done i'll open a small RFC for the fallback semantics (429 vs degrade).

Claudia: great. next check-in: Tuesday sync 09:30 PT. please drop short threads here if you hit blockers. closing this Slack thread, keeping follow-ups in the incident ticket and the new RFCs. :white_check_mark:
